newsitem.title: EGYPT: Faisal Islamic Bank raising capital, going majority foreign.
newsitem.headline: Faisal Islamic Bank raising capital, going majority foreign.

text.p: Faisal Islamic Bank of Egypt plans to raise its capital by $50 million and may allow foreign shareholders to own a majority stake, sources at the bank said on Sunday.
The bank now has capital of about $100 million and its statutes require the Egyptian shareholders to hold at least 51 percent of the equity.
The board has called an extraordinary general assembly for November 14 to approve the capital increase and abolish the restriction on foreign shareholders.
The sources said they expected most of the capital increase to come from the foreign shareholders, diluting the Egyptian shareholding to less than 50 percent.
The biggest foreign shareholders are Faisal Islamic Bank of Saudi Arabia and Geneva-based Dar al-Mal al-Islami, which is owned by Saudi interests.
An amendment to the Egyptian banking law earlier this year made it possible for the foreign partners in joint-venture banks to own more than 51 percent of the equity in the banks.
Faisal Islamic Bank of Egypt has a complicated share structure, with some shares denominated in pounds and some in dollars. The capital was also raised using different pound-dollar exchange rates.
